messages.subject: Instructions to counsel - Pennington (HSE investigation)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Clerks,

We should be grateful if Ms Stanford could advise Pennington Industries on exposure and sentencing strategy in an HSE matter (machinery guarding; serious injury). We attach the investigation report and forensic report under separate cover and would welcome a written advice and a conference. Please advise on availability and fee.

Tom Gallagher

--
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Instructions to counsel - Pennington (HSE investigation)
messages.plaintextBody:
Tom,

My advice is attached. In short: breach is not realistically defensible; the battle is culpability. I would resist high and press for medium - a maintenance lapse on a single machine against an otherwise functioning system - and accept harm category 2. On a medium organisation that points to a starting point of GBP 540,000 and, with the mitigation here, a figure before plea credit of the order of GBP 400,000, reducing to roughly GBP 266,000 with full credit. Strategy is to agree a basis of plea fixing those characterisations before any plea.

Harriet
